lines.ruling: Ruling: model error; i8889 p. 2, Last-month rule, "You may consider yourself an 'eligible individual' for the entire year if you are an eligible individual on the 1st day of the last month" (an election), and p. 4, Line 3, rule 2, "You are treated as having the same HDHP coverage for the entire year as you had on the first day of the last month"; amb.2025.hsa_last_month_all_year (chosen: the treatment applies to a filer who uses the rule; a filer eligible all year who does not keeps the actual family months). Triage .transcription/triage/2025/f8889.json (pass of this reply; 1,849 compared, 1,691 agree, 62 value differences, 14 on completed returns). The reply reads f8889.last_month only when fewer than 12 months were eligible, so a filer eligible all year with family coverage on December 1 is treated as family all year without the election (stage13.hsa_part_year_family, f8889.last_month false: $4,275.00 project v. $8,550.00); with the rule used and self-only on December 1 it still counts family months against rule 2 (stage11.hsa.last_month_changed $0 v. $2,850.00; stage13.mut.hsa_married_last_month_self_only $0 v. $4,275.00); for an unmarried filer 55 or older it adds the $1,000 to Step 1 (stage11.hsa.family_55 $8,550 v. $9,550), which Step 1 (family-coverage months only) does not include. Step 1 is read only for spouses with separate HSAs, so the only printed effect is line 6 on stage13.hsa_part_year_family (ruled at line 6). The project follows the source.
